Yuletide 2012

  • Profile

Welcome to Yuletide 2012, the 10th edition of the While We Tell of Yuletide Treasure Fanfiction Challenge. The stories are now live, and the authors are revealed!

Additional stories written to Yuletide 2012 prompts are now welcome in the New Year's Resolution 2013 challenge, which will remain open until next Yuletide. Please see that collection for the lists of prompts!
 

For more information and updates about Yuletide events, follow the Yuletide Admin LJ.

If you have any questions, please contact the mods at [email protected]

(Closed, Moderated, Gift Exchange Challenge)

Useful links

Basics

What is Yuletide?
Yuletide is an annual fic exchange for rare and obscure fandoms. Participants sign up to write a story of at least 1,000 words in a fandom someone else has requested. In return, they receive a story of at least 1,000 words in a fandom they have requested.

 

Who runs Yuletide?
The current mods are astolat and elynross. You can reach them at [email protected].

Where is Yuletide?
The stories
The Yuletide stories are available on on the Archive of Our Own (AO3) going back to 2009.

Earlier stories are available on the original Yuletide Treasure archive. They will eventually be imported into the AO3 to have the full collection in one place.

The challenge
The challenge is also run on the Archive of Our Own (AO3). The archive hosts nomination forms, signup forms, and story posting forms.

The information and announcements
• Information, scheduling, and admin announcements are made on the yuletide_admin Livejournal. You should follow this if you want to participate in the challenge. If you don't have a Livejournal, you can track the yuletide_admin RSS feed. (Right-click and copy that link into your feed reader.)

Participant discussions
Participants who have Livejournal accounts can post to the yuletide Livejournal. This is relatively low-volume during most of the year, but gets very busy around and just after Yuletide, with everything from planning posts to recs.

When does Yuletide happen?
The challenge takes place in the last few months of each year. Specific dates for each year are always announced in the yuletide_admin Livejournal and will also be listed on the challenge page for that year on the AO3.

General schedule:

  • Nominations: between late September and mid-October
  • Signups: between mid-October and mid-November
  • Assignments go out: sometime in November
  • Posting deadline: usually December 22, but possibly as early as December 19
  • Story reveal: December 25
  • Author reveal: January 1

How does Yuletide work?
Yuletide happens in four stages: Nominations, Signups, Assignments, Reveals.

During Nominations, people use a form on the AO3 to submit the names of three rare fandoms they want to request or write, with a few characters for each fandom. This results in a list of several thousand fandoms.

During Signups, people use a form on the AO3 to sign up to request and offer to write stories in fandoms from the nominated list. Participants must offer and request multiple fandoms to allow for better matching. But they are only required to write one story of at least 1,000 words. In return, they will receive one story of at least 1,000 words.

After signups, participants are matched up based on what they offered and requested, and Assignments are sent out. Participants have at least four weeks to write a story of at least 1,000 words.

Stories must be posted to the Yuletide challenge on the AO3 by the deadline, where they will automatically appear as anonymous "Mystery Gifts" for the recipients.

On December 25, the stories are Revealed, with author names still hidden.

On January 1, the author names are Revealed, and authors can begin answering comments if they wish.

Rules

Are there any rules?
Only a few:

  1. Write a complete story of at least 1,000 words, using a fandom and characters your recipient requested.
  2. If you realize you won't be able to finish, click the "default" button as soon as possible, so the mods can find a pinch hitter to fulfill your assignment.
  3. Post your completed story to the AO3 before the story deadline. Otherwise you'll be listed as having defaulted even if you intend to finish, and someone else will have to write an emergency last-minute pinch hit to be sure your recipient gets a story.
  4. Respect the anonymous nature of the challenge until after the author reveal on January 1: don't talk about what you're writing, and don't answer comments on the story you wrote until after the author reveal.

That's it! There are other traditions that have grown up around Yuletide over the years, but these four rules are all that's required of participants.

Rarity

How are you defining "rare"?
In 2012, these are the general guidelines used to disqualify fandoms:

  • Does it have 200+ stories of 1000+ words on the AO3?
  • Does it have 1000+ completed stories of 1000+ words in English on fanfiction.net?
  • Does the fandom have existing, fandom-specific archives of more than 500 stories?
  • Does it already have its own seasonal/holiday exchange?

Fandoms that meet at least two of these criteria are probably ineligible for Yuletide.

A major exception is fandoms that used to be large but that haven't had any new source material in the last ten+ years. If the fandom has largely died out as well, it may be eligible for Yuletide.

Participation

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

How do I participate?

  • You have to be over 18 years of age
  • You need an Archive of Our Own (AO3) account
  • You need to sign up for Yuletide on the AO3 during the signup period.

Signup time changes from year to year. To find out when to sign up, track the yuletide_admin Livejournal, which is where all admin announcements go.

 

 

What am I committing to if I sign up?
You're committing to writing one complete story of at least 1,000 words in a fandom your recipient requested, and using the characters they specified. Your recipient will match you on at least one of the fandoms and characters you offered, so it will be something you know you can write.

 

 

What if I don't have an AO3 account?
You can contact the mods at [email protected] before signups, and they'll issue you an invitation.

 

 

I don't want to sign up for the challenge, but still want to participate. How can I do that?
You can be a beta reader, cheer people on in chat, write Treats for any requests that catch your eye, or join the pinch hitter mailing list.  

 

I do want to sign up for the challenge, but I missed the signup window. Can I get in anyway?
Sorry, no. Everyone has to be signed up before the matching of writers & recipients, which happens right after signups close. You can still sign on to be a pinch hitter, though, or write Treats for people.

Nominations

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

How does nominating work?
At some point between late September and mid-October, the mods create a nominations form on the AO3 for the current year's challenge, and announce on the yuletide_admin Livejournal that nominations are open.

People who are planning to participate can nominate up to three fandoms that they want to be available for Yuletide, and up to four characters per fandom.

Here's a detailed tutorial on how to use the AO3's nominations form to nominate fandoms for Yuletide.

A group of people called "tag mods" work behind the scenes to check each fandom and its characters while the nominations are in process. They approve fandoms that are rare enough. They also reject fandoms that are too large, fandoms that have already been approved under other names, and characters that have already been approved under other names.

For example: "Sesame St." would be rejected if "Sesame Street (TV)" had already been nominated and approved.

Once nominations close, cleanup begins, and lasts about a week. First the mods go through the list of fandoms and characters and chase down duplicates and fix typos. Then they open up the list to public review for people to point out errors and corrections. By the end of this period, the list has been tightened into its final form and is ready for signups.

The challenge resets to zero every year: each year's participants create a brand-new list of fandoms and characters to choose from, based on what they want to read or write that year. So some fandoms show up almost every year, while others may only appear once.

 

Can I change my mind about my nominations after I submit them?
It's possible to change any of your nominations until that particular fandom or character gets approved or rejected. After that, you can't touch it any more.

With checking happening live behind the scenes, it's important to be sure of your nomination before you submit it. It's possible that a particular fandom or character has already been approved or rejected before you submit your nomination. In that case, you won't be able to change it.
 


 

Do I have to nominate fandoms to participate?
Nope! It's a good idea to nominate the fandoms you really want to see, though. There's no guarantee anyone else will nominate them, and the fandom list resets to zero every year. If no one nominates your fandom, it won't be available for Yuletide that year. But there's no obligation to nominate anything.
 

If I nominate fandoms, am I obligated to sign up?
No, there's no obligation to sign up, although the mods do ask that people only nominate if they're seriously considering signing up. Yuletide isn't designed to be a general prompt community where anyone can request stories. It's designed as a gift exchange, so the list of available fandoms should be one that active participants are specifically interested in.
 

 

What kind of fandoms can be nominated?
Any kind! Yuletide has had stories for western live action tv, k-drama, j-drama, cartoons, anime, reality shows, news shows, movies, novels, poems, manga, manhwa, manhua, comic books, comic strips, fairy tales, mythology, sacred texts, video games, webcomics, plays, commercials, songs, paintings, anthropomorfic, music videos, Youtube videos, and RPF from ancient history to today.

You name it, someone may well have requested it. As long as the fandoms are rare enough, you're good to go.

Signups

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

How do signups work?
Anyone over the age of 18 with an AO3 account can sign up for Yuletide. If you need an AO3 account, contact the mods at [email protected].

Here's a detailed tutorial for signing up for a challenge on AO3 – not specifically Yuletide, but all the basics are there.

The link to the signup form will be posted to the yuletide_admin LJ community, as well as the sidebar of the current year's Yuletide collection on AO3.

Requests

  • You have to request stories in at least three fandoms. You can add a fourth fandom if you want.
  • For each fandom, you can request 0 to 4 (nominated) characters.
  • If you request 0 characters, your writer is allowed to write about any of the nominated characters they want, or about the fandom universe in general.

Offers

  • You have to offer to write in at least four fandoms. You can add two more for a total of six fandoms, if you want.
  • In each fandom, you have to offer 2 to 8 nominated characters. You can also offer "Any" characters, but that really means any of the nominated characters, in any combination. If there are multiple fandoms where you're willing to write any of the nominated characters, you can make a "bucket offer".

Here's a brief guide to making a "bucket offer".

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

I won't be around during signups – can someone sign up for me?
Yes, you can use a signup proxy. This means allowing someone to have access to your AO3 account, so they can be logged in as you to fill in the signup form.

We recommend changing your password to something temporary if you want someone to sign you up for Yuletide, then changing it back again when you have time.

Can I change my mind about my signup after I submit it?
Yep! You can change your mind at any point during the signup period by editing your signup form. You can find your signup form on your AO3 profile page: click on "Signups" in the left-hand navigation pane.

I'm only comfortable with one or two of the fandoms on the list. Can I just offer/request those?
Sorry, no. For the matching to work, it's necessary to have a wider range of offers and requests. Otherwise, there's not enough flexibility in the system to match everyone.

 

I'm only comfortable with one of the characters in a fandom. Can I just offer that one?
Sorry, no. For the matching to work, it's necessary to have a wider range of offers. Otherwise, there's not enough flexibility in the system to match everyone.

I'm comfortable with lots of the fandoms on the list, and willing to write in even more. Can I offer as many as I want?
There's only one way to add extra fandoms to your offers: the "bucket offer", which is a group of fandoms for which you're willing to write absolutely any of the nominated characters.

Here's a brief guide to making a "bucket offer".

Otherwise, you're limited to a maximum of six offers. This is the flip side of the matching: too many possibilities makes the matching process too complicated, as every possible combination has to be considered.

If you want to write in more fandoms than the six you're limited to officially, you can write Treats for people after you've finished your assignment.

 


 

I'm comfortable with lots of the characters in a fandom. Can I offer more than eight?
There's only one way to add extra characters to your offers: selecting "Any". This means that you're willing to write absolutely any of the nominated characters in that fandom.

Otherwise, you're limited to a maximum of eight offers. This is the flip side of the matching: too many possibilities makes the matching process too complicated, as every possible combination has to be considered.
 


 

Can I veto certain topics/pairings/genres when I sign up?
No, there's no way to officially veto anything. Yuletide matching is based strictly on fandom and characters; nothing else is taken into consideration.

For your request, you can put a note in your "optional details" field or your "Dear Yuletide Writer" letter that you prefer some things more than others. Your author isn't required to take those notes into consideration, though. They're only required to write a story in the fandom you requested, using the characters you requested.

For your assignment, you're free to ignore whatever your recipient put in their optional details or "Dear Yuletide Writer" letter if you're not comfortable with their specific preferences. You're only obligated to write a complete story in one of the fandoms they requested using the characters they requested.

Write the story you're comfortable writing. If you can tailor it to at least approach your recipient's taste, that's great, but it's not required.

 

 

What if I didn't get a chance to nominate my favorite character, and I want to request them when I sign up?
Sorry, but the only characters available to request are the ones that were nominated. If you choose not to ask for any nominated characters at all, your writer can write about whichever of the nominated characters they want.

You're allowed to mention other characters in your "optional details" line, but your writer is free to ignore that and stick to just the officially nominated/requested characters.

What are "optional details"?
"Optional details" is the space on the form where you can give extra information about the kind of story you want to receive.

This information is optional for both you and your writer. You don't have to include anything here, and your writer doesn't have to include any of the details here in their story.

People generally use this space to give prompts; list the types of relationships that are okay, if any; and list their preferred tropes and dealbreakers. The idea is to give your author a direction to start in, while not demanding a specific storyline from them.
 

Here's a post that goes into detail about what sorts of prompts generally seem to work best for people, and why.
 

 
What if someone adds extra characters to the "optional details" line that I didn't offer to write?
Everything in the "optional details" line truly is optional. You're only required to write the characters they officially requested. If they ask for others, you can include them if you want, but are under no obligation to do so.

Assignments

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

How are assignments generated?
Once signups are over, the AO3's automated matching process will match up writers and recipients. As soon as everyone has a match both ways, you'll get an email with your assignment.

Your recipient is unlikely to be your writer, as the matching is almost never that direct. Usually you write for one person, and a different person writes for you.

You're only guaranteed to match your recipient on one fandom, although the matching process tries to match up people on more than one fandom.

The matching process is good, but not perfect. Most years, there's a handful of people who can't be matched up in one direction or the other. This means that some people will have more than one person officially assigned to write for them, and some people will see their request go out to the pinch hit list immediately.

 

 

I didn't get my assignment – what do I do?
It's possible that your spam filter ate the emailed assignment. Log in to your AO3 account and click the link for "Assignments" in the left-hand navigation pane in your Profile; your assignment should be there.

If it's not there, either, please contact the mods immediately at [email protected].

 

 
Can I switch my assignment?
Assignments can't be changed under most circumstances.

 If you signed up for one of the fandoms your recipient requested, you were matched appropriately. This means you are obligated to write them a story, even if you signed up for that fandom accidentally. You're free to write in any of the fandoms they requested, and to ignore their "optional details" field.

The only exception is if you were assigned a fandom you definitely didn't sign up for. Please check your signup to confirm - you can find it on your AO3 profile page under "Assignments" in the left-hand navigation pane. In that case, contact the mods as soon as possible at [email protected], and let them know.
 

 
Do I have to write stories for all of my recipient's requests?
Nope! You're only required to write one story, and you can choose which of their requested fandoms to write it in.

 

 
Can I write a story in any of my recipient's fandoms, even if I didn't sign up for them?
Sure! As long as you write a story for one of the fandoms they requested, you're good.

 
Can I write more than one story?
Sure! First you have to write a complete story of at least 1,000 words in one of your recipient's fandoms, using the characters they requested. After that, you can write as many stories as you want, for your recipient or for other people.

 

 
Am I guaranteed to be the only person writing a story for my recipient?
No, there's no way to guarantee that. Most years at least one person has two officially assigned authors, simply to make the matching work.

Beyond that, everyone is free to write as many stories as they want, for whoever they want, as long as they write their assigned story first. If your recipient has a request that catches someone else's eye, they may get an extra story or two.
 

 
Will I get more than one story?
Probably not. Despite the popularity of Treat-writing among some Yuletiders, most participants get one story, just as most participants write one story.

Posting

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

How do I post my story?
Go to your Assignment page on AO3, which you can find under the "Assignments" link on your Profile page, or on the Yuletide subcollection page as "Your Assignment". You should see two buttons at the bottom of your Yuletide assignment: "Post to fulfill", and "Default".

Click "Post to fulfill", and you'll be taken to a posting form. This will automatically post your story into the current year's Yuletide challenge. It also has your recipient's name already filled in. All you need to do is fill in the rest of the form, preview it to make sure it looks okay, and post.

If you're posting a Treat, you won't have an assignment or "post to fulfill" button. Instead, go to the current challenge page on the AO3, and click on "Post To Collection" under the challenge title. This will take you to a form with the challenge collection name already filled in. Fill in the recipient's name manually, then fill in the rest of the form, preview it to make sure it looks okay, and post.

Treats that are at least 1,000 words should be posted in the main Yuletide collection for that year.

Treats that are under 1,000 words should be posted in the Yuletide Madness collection for that year, once it opens.

Here's a detailed guide to uploading Yuletide stories to AO3 -- this was written in 2009, and a few things have been simplified since then. But it has lots of screencaps to help you fill out the posting form if you're not used to it.

 

 
Can someone else post my story for me?
Yes, you can use a "proxy uploader" to post your story. There are two ways to do this:

  1. Give someone access to your account so they can log in as you and upload your story.
  • We recommend changing your password to something temporary for this, and then changing it back later.

  • Find someone who has an AO3 account and is willing to upload your story for you, and send them your story with all the information they'll need to fill in the posting form.

    • The proxy uploader will upload the story under their own AO3 account, and list your AO3 pseud as a co-author.
    • Once it's uploaded, the proxy uploader edits the story to remove their name as author.
    • You are now listed as the sole author of the story, and the proxy uploader no longer has access to it. They can't edit or change it in any way.

     

     

     

     

     

     

     

     

     

     

    Can I post my story before the deadline?
    Sure! The posting form opens shortly after assignments go out. You're free to post whenever you want.
     


     

    Can I edit my story after it's posted?
    Yes, the AO3 allows editing at any time.

     

     
    Can I add author's notes?
    You can, but they will be visible as soon as the stories are revealed on December 25. Be careful not to put anything here that would give away your identity.

    Defaulting

     

     

     

     

     

     

     

     

     

     

    What if I can't finish my story?
    If you can't finish in time, you can default. This lets the mods know they need to find a pinch hitter to write a story for your recipient.

    To default, go to your Assignment page on AO3, which you can find under the "Assignments" link on your Profile page, or on the Yuletide subcollection page as "Your Assignment". You should see two buttons at the bottom of your Yuletide assignment: "Post to fulfill", and "Default".

    Click the Default button, then click the confirmation on the popup that appears. The mods will be notified and will find a pinch hitter to fulfill your assignment.

     

     

    What happens if I default?
    Whether you get a penalty for defaulting depends on how and when you default.

    • Before December 16: If you default using the AO3 button before 11:59 pm Eastern US time on December 15 (What time is that where I am?), you'll be flagged as a defaulter, but with no penalty.
    • After December 15 but before December 20: If you default by using the Default button after December 15, but before the deadline on December 20, you should write to the mods at [email protected]. They may ask you to write and post another story before the next year's signups start, if you want to participate again.
    • No-show default: If you default by simply failing to post your story, without using the Default button or writing to the mods in advance, you will be banned from future Yuletides. Also, bears will eat you.
    • Multiple defaults: Multiple defaults may also result in your being banned, even if you did use the Default button or write to the mods.

    Pinch hits

     

     

     

     

     

     

     

     

     

     

    What are pinch hits?
    Pinch hits are assignments that the original author has had to default on, or rarely, assignments that couldn't be matched to any authors. As people default, elynross posts the assignments to the pinch-hit mailing list, where they're available for anyone to claim.

    Pinch hits are one of the most popular parts of Yuletide, and there's a lot of competition to get them. There are currently more people signed up on the pinch-hit list than sign up for Yuletide proper.
     

     
    Do I need to be signed up for Yuletide to be a pinch hitter?
    Nope! Anyone with an AO3 account can sign up to be a pinch hitter. If you want to be a pinch hitter and don't have an AO3 account, contact the mods at [email protected].
     

     
    How do I become a pinch hitter?
    Sign up for the Yuletide Pinch Hitters mailing list on Yahoo groups. You can do that on the website, or by email:

    • On the web: Click "join this group". You need to have or create a Yahoo account to join via the web.
    • By email: Send a blank email to [email protected].
      • To activate your subscription, just reply to the confirmation message you receive from the group.

    And that's it – once you're on the list, you'll receive the pinch hit messages, and can try to claim any pinch hits that catch your eye.

     

     
    How do I claim a pinch hit?
    Keep an eye on your email. Pinch hits are generally sent out in batches, starting with a small flurry in the first week or two, then a slow trickle until the final couple of weeks before the deadline, where there's often a dozen or more a day.

    If you see one that interests you, hit reply on the email, and send it without changing the subject line in any way. You can say that you want the pinch hit in the body of the email message, but do not change the subject line beyond the "Re:" your email program adds automatically.

    Pinch hits go very fast – many within minutes – so act fast if you see something you want and are willing to commit to.

    If you're the first one to request that pinch hit, elynross will respond and let you know it's yours. You'll be able to see it listed on your AO3 profile page by clicking "Assignments" in the left-hand navigation pane. If elynross doesn't respond to you, you didn't get it.
     

     
    What am I committing to if I claim a pinch hit?
    You're committing to write a complete story of at least 1,000 words in one of the recipient's chosen fandoms and using their chosen character(s).

    For pinch hits that are assigned before December 10, the deadline is the same as the regular deadline: 8:00 pm (ET) on December 20. (What time is that where I am?)

    For pinch hits that are assigned after December 10, the deadline is December 24, but uploading earlier is better.

     

     
    Can I write a pinch hit even if I wasn't officially assigned to it?
    Sure! In that case, it would be a Treat.

    • If it's 1,000 words or more, upload it to the regular Yuletide subcollection for that year. You can post it whenever it's ready.
    • If it's under 1,000 words, upload it to the Yuletide Madness subcollection for that year. You'll have to wait till Madness opens to upload your story.

     

     

     

     

     

     

     

     

     

     

    How do I post my pinch hit?
    Go to your Assignment page on AO3, which you can find under the "Assignments" link on your Profile page, or on the Yuletide subcollection page as "Your Assignment". You should see two buttons at the bottom of your Yuletide assignment: "Post to fulfill", and "Default".

    Click "Post to fulfill", and you'll be taken to a posting form. This will automatically post your story into the current year's Yuletide challenge. It also has your recipient's name already filled in. All you need to do is fill in the rest of the form, preview it to make sure it looks okay, and post.

    If you're posting a Treat, you won't have an assignment or "post to fulfill" button. Instead, go to the current challenge page on the AO3, and click on "Post To Collection" under the challenge title. This will take you to a form with the challenge collection name already filled in. Fill in the recipient's name manually, then fill in the rest of the form, preview it to make sure it looks okay, and post.

    Here's a detailed guide to uploading Yuletide stories to AO3 -- this was written in 2009, and a few things have been simplified since then. But it has lots of screencaps to help you fill out the posting form if you're not used to it.

    Yuletide Madness

    Yuletide Madness happens in the last 24-48 hours of the challenge. It's a way of making sure that all participants have a story waiting for them in the archive.

    When Madness first opens, the requests from people who do not yet have a gift story waiting in the archive are made public, even though pinch hitters have been assigned to them already. Any participant who wants to is free to write and post a 1,000+ word story for any of the requests. This is a safety net, in case an assigned pinch hitter has to default.

    Once everyone definitely has at least one 1,000-word gift in the archive, Madness is thrown wide open to all requests, and the Madness subcollection is opened, for stories of under 1,000 words. At that point, anyone can write whatever they want for any request they want.

    Stories that are more than 1,000 words should be posted to the regular Yuletide collection. Stories that are under 1,000 words should be posted to the Madness collection.

    Reveals

    Reveals come in two stages: story reveals, and author reveals.

    Story reveals
    On December 25, the mods switch all the regular Yuletide stories for that year from hidden to visible. As soon as that happens, participants are automatically notified by email that they have a gift waiting for them, with a link directly to their gift story. Participants can also look on their AO3 profile under "Gifts" to find their gift story. Author names are still hidden at this point.

    On December 26, the mods switch all the Yuletide Madness stories for that year from hidden to visible. Anyone who has a story waiting for them in Madness is automatically notified by email that they have a gift waiting for them, with a link directly to their gift story. Participants can also look on their AO3 profile under "Gifts" to find their gift story. Author names are still hidden at this point.

    Author reveals
    On January 1, the mods switch all the Yuletide stories for that year from anonymous to showing author names. Everyone can see who wrote the stories.

    Once author names have been revealed, participants can respond to comments on the stories they wrote.

    Extras

    Dear Yuletide Writer letters
    "Dear Yuletide Writer" letters (also known as Dear Yuletide Author, Dear Yuletide Santa, etc.) are letters posted to journals or other spaces that give your writer a bit more information about why you picked the sources you did, what your likes and dislikes are, more detailed prompts, and so forth.

    Like the "optional details" field, DYW letters are entirely optional. You don't have to write one, and you're free to ignore your recipient's letter while writing your story.

    People who choose to write a DYW letter can put the link in their signups, so their authors can find it easily. They can also add the link to a DYW post in the Yuletide LJ comm.

    You can find the most recent year's post linked in the top sidebar on the main Yuletide LJ community, or by checking the dear yuletide writer tag.
     

    IRC chat
    There's a Yuletide IRC chat room set up every year. Anyone who wants to can go hang out to cheer each other on, panic to a sympathetic audience, ask for betas, etc.

    server: irc.sff.net (standalone server)
    room: #yuletide
    no password needed

     
    Here's a detailed post on how the YT chat works and how to join it.

     

    Beta readers
    A beta reader is someone who reads your story and gives you feedback to help improve it. There are a few ways to connect potential beta readers with authors for Yuletide.

    First, there's always a post in the Yuletide LJ comm where people willing to beta can leave a comment with their name, fandoms they can beta in, and types of beta they provide, so authors can contact them. You can check the "beta readers" tag on the Yuletide LJ comm to find the current year's beta-reader post.

    Second, there's the IRC chat. Since Yuletide is all about the anonymity, the folks in the chat room have come up with a way to use middlemen – known as "hippos" – to connect authors and betas.

    You can private message someone with "hippo" in front of their name and they'll announce in the chat room that a beta is needed for your fandom, check back with you to make sure anyone volunteering isn't your recipient, and then have the beta message you.
     

    Here's a detailed guide explaining the whole Hippo thing and how it works.

    Third, and as a last resort if nothing else has worked, you can email the mods at [email protected]. They'll check to see if whoever else offered your fandom during signups is available to beta.

     

    Treats
    Treats are just that: unassigned extra stories written for the fun of it.

    People whose requests go out to the pinch hit list in the last week of the challenge are the most likely to get treats written for them as people scramble to make sure everyone is covered. But anyone whose request goes to the pinch hit list at all or who posts a Dear Yuletide Writer letter and links it at the Yuletide LJ comm may find an extra gift in the archive for them on story reveal day.

    There's no way to differentiate an assigned story from a Treat in the archive. Some treat-writers put something in the author's notes about this being a treat so the recipient will know which is their official gift.

    If you're writing a Treat, you won't have an assignment or "post to fulfill" button. Instead, go to the current challenge page on the AO3, and click on "Post To Collection" under the challenge title. This will take you to a form with the challenge collection name already filled in. Fill in the recipient's name manually, then fill in the rest of the form, preview it to make sure it looks okay, and post.

    • Treats that are over 1,000 words should be posted to the regular Yuletide subcollection for that year.
    • Treats of under 1,000 words should be posted into the Yuletide Madness collection. It opens roughly a day before the story reveal, once every single participant has a 1,000+ word gift story waiting for them in the archive.

    Here's a detailed guide to uploading Yuletide stories to AO3 -- this was written in 2009, and a few things have been simplified since then (for example, if you use the "post to fulfill" button, you won't have to fill in the challenge name), but it has lots of screencaps of how to fill out the posting form if you're not used to it.

    New Year's Resolution challenge
    The New Year's Resolution challenge opens on January 1, after author reveals go live. The challenge remains open until the next Yuletide signups close.

    All of the requests that were submitted for the most recent Yuletide are made available. Anyone with an AO3 account can write stories for them and post them into that year's NYR subcollection. So, for instance, after Yuletide 2011 closed, those prompts were made available for NYR 2012.
